title: Welcome to My Office: The Story of This Portfolio

pages.heading: A portfolio with no menu
lines: People often compliment my office when they see it behind me on video calls. It's full of things that say who I am, so I put the same things in my portfolio: click an object and it tells you about my work.
**Role:** Concept, design and art direction
**Built with:** Claude Design (prototype and 3D objects) and Claude Code (the site)
**Stack:** React, TypeScript, three.js
**Timeline:** Sep – Oct 2026

pages.heading: Why an office
lines: Most portfolios look alike: a grid of thumbnails and an About page. I wanted mine to feel like me.
So the home is my real office, with the same bookcase, plant, globe, chess set, cat and pink phone. There's no navigation bar: you explore, and each thing you find opens a piece of my story.
For anyone in a hurry, a small menu lists everything too.

poll.title: A quick guess
poll.question: How many things can you click in this office?
poll.reveal: 17 objects to discover, plus the moon lamp, which changes the light. The first prototype already promised “0 of 17 discovered”, and with this book on the shelf, the office finally lives up to it.

pages.heading: The real thing
lines: Everything on the shelf is something I own: the yellow bookcase, the plant, the moon lamp, the chess board, my diploma tube, the llama bank and the Johnny Cash poster. And Zuko, of course.
Keeping it real was the point. The portfolio is my office, so the details had to be mine, down to the colour of the shelves.

pages.heading: From a sketch to a real site
lines: It started on paper: a quick sketch of the wall, the shelf and the bookcase, with notes on what each thing would open.
I took it to **Claude Design** to prototype the room and model the 3D objects, then moved to **Claude Code** to build the site for real, with real content, real interactions and a phone version.

pages.heading: From my office to 3D
lines: After the sketch, I designed the room in **Claude Design**, where I also modelled the main objects in 3D, starting with the bookcase. Drag it around.

Then I moved to **Claude Code** to build the real site. I directed the work end to end: the concept, the content, how each object behaves and every visual detail, reviewing each change on desktop and on a phone.

pages.heading: Every object has a job
lines: Each object opens something that fits it. The globe spins to the countries I've visited, the phone dials my contacts, and the diploma tube unrolls my real diploma.
The cork board holds notes from mentees, the postcard flips to say where I'm from, and Zuko, my cat, answers questions about my work.
Try them from here:

pages.heading: The same room, in your hand
lines: On a phone, the whole office still fits the screen. You pinch and drag to look around, tap once to name an object and tap again to open it.
I audited it like any product: small objects got an invisible touch area, every button became at least 44px, no text is smaller than 12px, and nothing that opens needs scrolling.

pages.heading: Telling each case its own way
lines: The words live in Notion and sync into the books. The cases are told with pages built for them, so you do something on each one: answer a quiz, flip a card, compare versions, watch a number move.
Those pieces are reusable, so every new case can pick the ones that tell its story best.

showcase.title: Open the office
